Outcome 1 of 3

Disruption recovery: one storm, one night

A storm strands 212 arriving guests. Recovered in minutes, not hours.

CoworkDynamics 365 Contact CenterDynamics 365 Customer ServiceCopilot Studio

1The persona

Amara OkaforDuty Manager, Contoso Airport Hotel
When the airport closes, I have 212 guests, one phone line and no single picture of who needs what.
Goals
  • Every guest has a bed tonight
  • Fair, consistent comp decisions
  • Keep the front desk calm
Frustrations
  • Guest data is split across the property system, email and the phone
  • Calls guests one by one while the line keeps ringing
  • Comp decided shift by shift, with no clear policy view

2The problem

Recovery runs on phones, spreadsheets and goodwill

Weather, cancelled flights and oversold nights happen every week somewhere in a portfolio. Each one turns into hours of manual work, inconsistent comp and frustrated loyalty members, and leadership hears about it days later.

Hoursto know which guests are affected
1 by 1guest calls from the front desk
Next daybefore revenue management reacts
Days laterbefore any review happens

The process, start to finish

  1. 1DetectCoworkStorm, flight and occupancy signals become one briefing
  2. 2PlanCowork + Duty ManagerWho stays, who moves, what each guest is offered
  3. 3Reach every guestAgent + Contact CenterRebook, extend, comp and shuttle on every channel
  4. 4Handle exceptionsCustomer ServiceAccessibility, VIP and complaints routed with context
  5. 5Protect revenueCowork + RevenueStranded demand and new rates
  6. 6ReviewCowork + CEOCost, sentiment and an updated playbook

4Better together

Dynamics 365

Runs the transaction: guest records, loyalty, cases and every booking change, in Contact Center and Customer Service.

Agents

Does the work around the clock: reaches 212 guests at once, rebooks, applies comp and books the shuttle.

Cowork

Where people direct the work: the briefing, the plan, the approval, the dashboards and the morning review.

Take Dynamics away and the agent has nothing to act on. Take the agent away and Amara is back on the phone. Take Cowork away and nobody can see, steer or approve the whole recovery.

Today

  • Guests called one by one

  • Review days later, if at all
With Cowork, Dynamics 365 and agents
  • Briefing waiting before the phones ring
  • One approved plan, carried out for every guest
  • Comp applied by policy and tier
  • Rates adjusted the same night
  • CEO briefing and playbook by 7:00 AM

Questions to start the conversation

  • What happened the last time weather or an oversell hit one of your properties?
  • How long does it take to know which guests are affected?
  • Who decides comp, and how consistent is it?
  • How many of those guests could have been served without a call?
  • When does revenue management find out?
  • What does leadership see the next morning?

Also fits Airlines: irregular operations and rebooking. Cruise lines: itinerary changes and port swaps.

By the time I rebuild a proposal from old files, the planner has already heard from two other hotels.

  • Proposals rebuilt by hand from old documents

2The problem

Big revenue, run on email and copy-paste

Groups and events are among a hotel's largest revenue streams, yet RFPs sit in shared inboxes, proposals are rebuilt by hand, event orders change in email threads, and the master bill turns into weeks of disputes.

Daysto answer an RFP
Manualspace and displacement checks
Email threadsfor event changes
Weeksto settle the master bill

Procure-to-pay and prime cost: from the dock to the GM's Monday

From the receiving dock to a Monday food and labor cost view for the GM.

CoworkDynamics 365 Supply Chain ManagementDynamics 365 FinanceCopilot Studio

1The persona

Sofia BianchiDirector of Food and Beverage, Contoso Downtown
I find out a supplier raised prices after we have already paid three invoices at the new rate.
Goals
  • Hit food cost targets every week
  • Pay suppliers right, the first time
  • Spend time on guests, not paperwork
Frustrations
  • Deliveries, orders and invoices rarely line up
  • Accounts payable matches paper by hand
  • Cost reports arrive weeks after month end

2The problem

The biggest controllable costs, seen too late

Food, beverage and labor are a hotel's largest controllable costs. Purchase orders, deliveries and invoices rarely line up, accounts payable spends days matching paper, and the GM sees the variance weeks after it happened.

Dayseach month matching invoices
After paymentprice changes discovered
Weeksuntil cost reports arrive
Last monthis what the GM reacts to

The process, start to finish

  1. 1OrderSupply ChainPar levels and menus drive purchase orders
  2. 2ReceiveChef + F&BDelivery checked against the order
  3. 3MatchAgentOrder, receipt and invoice matched
  4. 4ResolveAgent + AP + CoworkExceptions explained, supplier note drafted
  5. 5PayDynamics 365 FinanceApproved invoices paid on terms
  6. 6ReviewCowork + GMMonday prime cost with actions
